name: Huntsman

logo.source: huntsman.com site header logo (theme/images/logo.svg); Wikipedia infobox file Huntsman Corporation - Logo.svg was rate-limited

description: Huntsman makes organic chemicals, mostly for insulation, cars, adhesives and aircraft. The biggest business, Polyurethanes (65 percent of segment revenue), makes MDI, the chemical that is mixed with polyols to make rigid insulation foam, car seat cushioning and footwear, and it earns thin margins that swing with China and construction demand. Performance Products makes amines and maleic anhydride for epoxy hardeners, fuel additives and fiberglass resins. Advanced Materials sells epoxy and similar formulations to aerospace, electrical and electronics customers and has the best margin. 2025 revenue was $5.7 billion and the company lost $227 million; in November 2025 it cut its dividend 65 percent, and in June 2026 it agreed an all-stock merger with Olin (stockholders approved on August 25, 2026; closing expected in the first half of 2027).

hq.note: 10003 Woodloch Forest Drive, The Woodlands, Texas 77380 (FY2025 10-K Item 1)

employees.note: "approximately 6,000 associates", about 2,000 in the US and 4,000 elsewhere (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Polyurethanes
businessLines.how: Sells MDI and polyols by the pound, and increasingly pre-blended 'systems', to insulation, automotive, furniture and footwear manufacturers; price is set by the global MDI supply-demand balance, so margins are thin and cyclical.
businessLines.description: MDI, polyols, TPU and other polyurethane products, plus Huntsman Building Solutions (spray polyurethane foam insulation). Three world-scale MDI plants in Geismar (Louisiana), Rotterdam and Caojing (China); 14 formulation 'systems houses'.

revenue.note: Segment revenue before eliminations; FY2024 $3,900M; FY2023 $3,865M

businessLines.revenueNote: Segment revenue before eliminations; FY2024 $3,900M; FY2023 $3,865M

operatingProfit.note: Segment adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP); FY2024 $245M; FY2023 $248M. About 35.3% of the $414M segment total before corporate costs of $(139)M

businessLines.name: Performance Products
businessLines.how: Specialty and intermediate chemicals sold by the pound to lubricant-additive, fuel-additive, epoxy, coatings and resin makers; amines are priced on performance in the application rather than on raw materials, maleic anhydride follows capacity use and feedstock cost.
businessLines.description: Performance amines (polyetheramines, DGA, JEFFCAT catalysts, E-GRADE semiconductor amines), ethyleneamines, and maleic anhydride; seven amines plants and two maleic anhydride plants in North America.

operatingProfit.note: Segment adjusted EBITDA; FY2024 $153M; FY2023 $201M. About 25.8% of the segment total

businessLines.name: Advanced Materials
businessLines.how: Custom-formulated resins and curing agents qualified into customers' aircraft, power equipment and electronics products, sold by the pound at prices set by performance and long qualification, so margins are higher than the commodity-like lines.
businessLines.description: Epoxy, phenoxy, acrylic, polyurethane and acrylonitrile-butadiene-based polymer formulations, high-performance thermoset resins, curing and toughening agents, and carbon nanotube additives.

operatingProfit.note: Segment adjusted EBITDA; FY2024 $179M; FY2023 $186M. About 38.9% of the segment total, the largest share from the smallest segment

brands.name: Huntsman Building Solutions (spray polyurethane foam insulation)
Rubicon LLC (with Lanxess; aniline, nitrobenzene and DPA at Geismar)
brands.share: Huntsman is entitled to about 78% of nitrobenzene and aniline capacity; Lanxess to all DPA

brands.name: Huntsman Polyurethanes Shanghai (HPS, MDI joint venture with Shanghai Chlor-Alkali)
